title: Grade 3 Math — Fri, Jun 27
description: Fractions — Day 5 of 5: Mixed review — fractions in pictures and word problems
subject: mathematics

questions.question: In the fraction 5/9, the numerator is ___ and denominator is ___.
questions.explanation: In 5/9: top number (5) = numerator; bottom number (9) = denominator.

questions.question: Which is the largest unit fraction: 1/2, 1/7, 1/4, 1/9?
questions.explanation: For unit fractions, larger denominator = smaller fraction. So 1/2 is the largest here.

questions.question: A pie is divided into 8 equal pieces. Sam eats 3, Mary eats 2. What fraction is left?
Which pair are like fractions?
questions.explanation: 3/8 and 5/8 both have denominator 8 — they are like fractions.

questions.question: A ribbon is 1 metre long. Priya cuts 3/10 of it. What fraction remains?
Arrange 3/11, 8/11, 5/11 in DECREASING order:
questions.explanation: Same denominator (11). Decreasing by numerator: 8 > 5 > 3. Order: 8/11, 5/11, 3/11.

questions.question: If 1/6 of a bag = 4 candies, how many candies are in the whole bag?
questions.explanation: 1/6 = 4 candies. Total = 6 × 4 = 24 candies in the whole bag.

questions.question: Mohan has done 3/8 of his work and his brother has done 5/8. Together, what fraction is done?
questions.explanation: 3/8 + 5/8 = 8/8 = 1 whole. Together they have completed ALL the work.

questions.question: What fraction of the week (7 days) are the 5 school days?
questions.explanation: 5 school days out of 7 total days = 5/7.

questions.question: A class has 24 students. 9 are absent. What fraction of students are PRESENT?
Kavita read 2/9 of a book today and 4/9 yesterday. What fraction has she NOT yet read?
A number line goes from 0 to 1. Fractions 1/5, 2/5, 3/5, 4/5 divide it. How many equal parts are between 0 and 1?
questions.explanation: The denominator (5) tells us the number of equal parts. The number line is divided into 5 equal parts: 0, 1/5, 2/5, 3/5, 4/5, 1.

questions.question: 3 friends share a pizza. One eats 3/12, another eats 5/12, the third eats 4/12. Have they eaten the whole pizza?
options: No — 13/12 which is more than a whole
questions.explanation: 3/12 + 5/12 + 4/12 = 12/12? No: 3 + 5 + 4 = 12. Wait: yes! 12/12 = 1. Actually they ate the whole pizza. Let me recalculate: 3+5+4 = 12. So 12/12 = 1. But option A says 11/12... Hmm, 3+5+4 = 12, so they ate the whole pizza (12/12). Option B is correct.
3/12 + 5/12 + 4/12: add numerators 3 + 5 + 4 = 12. So 12/12 = 1 whole. Yes, they ate the entire pizza.

questions.question: Which fraction is between 1/2 and 1 on the number line?
questions.explanation: 3/4 = 0.75, which is between 1/2 (=0.5) and 1. The others — 1/4, 1/3, 1/5 — are all less than 1/2.
